The Opportunity
The Problem Worth Solving

Churches cycle through worship leaders every two to three years. Every new hire arrives as a stranger to the culture, earns trust slowly, reaches peak effectiveness, and then begins thinking about what's next. Then the search starts over.

The cost is real: a staffing firm placement runs 15–20% of first-year salary, and most external hires don't outlast year three. More importantly, the congregation endures repeated disruption — new faces, new styles, new visions for Sunday. Meanwhile, there are people who already know the church, already love the people, and are already faithfully sitting in the rows every week. They simply haven't been asked to step up.

The Core Insight
The next worship leader for your church may already be in your congregation. Win the Week helps you find them, develop them, and set them up to last.
About the Program
What Win the Week Does

Win the Week works alongside a church to identify a faithful volunteer — already on your worship team or in your chairs — someone the congregation already knows and trusts, who simply hasn't been asked to lead yet. Then we develop them into a capable, sustainable worship leader.

The engagement combines a proven framework, direct coaching, practical tools, and a structured development pathway tailored to your church's context.

"The next worship leader for your church may already be in the front row."

Casey leading worship at his last church — every person on the frontline is a leader he developed.

Full Engagement
Program Scope

Every church engagement includes:

  • Discovery & Team Assessment
    Identifying the right candidate(s) from your existing worship team
  • Win the Week Framework Training
    Teaching the 5-hour weekly workflow that prevents burnout and builds consistency
  • 1-on-1 Coaching Sessions
    Weekly calls with Casey directly coaching the developing leader
  • Sunday Execution Mentorship
    Practical guidance on planning, leading, and running Sunday services
  • Team Communication Tools
    Templates and systems for coordinating volunteers and managing rehearsals
  • Spiritual Formation Touchpoints
    Equipping them not just to execute but to lead with pastoral presence
  • Senior Pastor Integration
    Regular check-ins with church leadership to align development with the church's vision
  • Final Evaluation & Handoff
    A documented readiness assessment and formal transition to independent leadership
  • Case Study Documentation
    A written account of the engagement for your church's records and the Win the Week library
  • Lifetime Win the Week Community Access Included
    When the engagement ends, your worship leader isn't on their own. They keep access to the Win the Week community — a growing network of worship leaders sharing wins, working through challenges, and doing weekly peer check-ins together. No ongoing fee. No expiration.
The Journey
Your Church's Sequence

A standard engagement runs 4–6 months. Here is what that looks like from the church's perspective:

1
Discovery & Alignment
Weeks 1–2

Casey meets with church leadership and the worship team to understand the culture, assess current health, and identify the right candidate(s). Shared expectations are established between Casey, the candidate, and the senior pastor — including the compensation pathway, so every party enters the engagement with eyes open.

  • Kickoff call with senior pastor or executive pastor
  • Worship team assessment (observation + interviews)
  • Candidate identification and commitment conversation
  • Compensation pathway defined in writing — volunteer during the engagement, part-time hire upon completion, with agreed milestones for full-time growth
  • Candidate enters willingly and informed — no surprises on either side
  • Development goals established in writing
2
Foundation
Weeks 3–6

The candidate begins learning the Win the Week framework. Casey introduces the 5-hour weekly planning workflow, Sunday execution tools, and the rhythms that keep a worship leader from burning out.

  • Win the Week framework onboarding (sessions 1–3)
  • First solo planning cycle (with oversight)
  • Introduction to team communication systems
  • Weekly 1-on-1 coaching calls with Casey
3
Development
Weeks 7–14

The core growth phase, structured around the Gradual Release of Responsibility (GRR) — a proven instructional model that moves ownership from coach to leader in four deliberate steps: You Watch Me Do → You Help Me Do → I Help You Do → I Watch You Do. Coaching begins weekly and tapers to bi-weekly as the candidate moves through each stage and builds confidence leading independently. The senior pastor enters the loop here with regular check-ins — this is where real alignment between pastor and worship leader gets forged.

  • Weekly 1-on-1 coaching with Casey (tapering to bi-weekly as GRR progresses)
  • Leading full Sunday services (planning to execution)
  • Volunteer team coordination
  • Weekly pastor / worship leader check-ins — building direct trust and accountability
  • Bi-weekly pastor check-ins with Casey — progress reports, wins, and concerns
  • Mid-engagement review with senior pastor
4
Integration
Weeks 15–20

The candidate now functions as a worship leader with Casey as an ongoing sounding board. This phase focuses on sustainability: building habits that last, navigating team dynamics, and deepening the pastoral dimension of their role.

  • Weekly coaching resumes — covering the topics that go beyond execution
  • Independent Sunday ownership with Casey as sounding board
  • Advanced scenario coaching — team conflict, low attendance, creative ruts
  • Discipling new leaders — "who's on your bench?" building the next layer of the team
  • Peer cohort introduction (other developing leaders)
5
Handoff & Launch
Weeks 21–24

The engagement closes with a formal evaluation, a celebration of the work done, and everything documented. The leader is ready. The church has a case study. Casey has a story to tell.

  • Final readiness assessment
  • Senior pastor sign-off conversation
  • Case study written and delivered
  • Video testimonial (if applicable)
  • Lifetime access to the Win the Week community — peer worship leaders, no fee

Placement vs. Development
These Aren't the Same Thing

A staffing firm's job is placement. They screen candidates, make the match, hand the leader over — and that's where their involvement ends. Win the Week does something categorically different. It builds a leader from within your own congregation: months of hands-on coaching, practical development, and intentional formation. When the engagement ends, you have a leader who is proven, already trusted by your people, with a growing bench behind them — and they're never left on their own after that.

The cost difference is real, but it's almost beside the point. You're not choosing between two ways to hire. You're choosing between filling a seat and building a ministry.

The Candidate's Compensation Path
A Clear Deal for the Person Being Developed

The person going through this training is a real human being with real expectations. Win the Week establishes a clear, written compensation pathway in Phase 1 — before anyone commits — so the candidate knows exactly what they're agreeing to and what they're working toward. No surprises. No bait and switch. The church defines the numbers; Win the Week makes sure it's all in writing before the engagement begins.

During the Engagement
Volunteer
By written agreement with the candidate — entered willingly, with full knowledge of what comes next.
Upon Completion
Part-Time Hire
The church makes a formal offer. Not a possibility — a commitment defined before the engagement begins.
Growing Into
Full-Time
Based on milestones and church needs — defined in writing during Phase 1, not decided after the fact.
